description: Check whether a Pulse signed price print is authentic and unaltered — pass a print back exactly as a Pulse tool returned it and this recomputes the ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256 signature over the canonical string, entirely OFFLINE with no network call to Pulse. WHAT A valid:true RESULT PROVES: that Pulse asserted this exact price, for this symbol, at this timestamp, at this grade, and that nobody altered any of those fields in transit — it detects a single changed digit of price or a one-millisecond shift in the timestamp. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE: that the price is CORRECT or reflects the true market — this checks Pulse's signature, not the world, so a print can verify perfectly and still be a price Pulse itself got wrong. The verification is computed here, not asked of Pulse, so Pulse cannot vouch for a print it never signed and an offline or compromised source cannot turn an invalid print into a valid one. Needs NO API key. Example: pulse_verify_print({ symbol: "BTC", priceText: "76051.0676303142", price: 76051.0676303142, at: "2026-09-16T23:39:30.524Z", grade: "consensus", signature: "wiD005d9...", kid: "pvi-Sl40p5Gj2t_-JyKUhxyg" }).

at.description: From the print, unchanged. A 1ms difference invalidates the signature.

grade.description: From the print: consensus, blended or indicative.

kid.description: Key id from the print; selects which public key to check against.

price.description: From the print. Used only if priceText is absent.

priceText.description: The price EXACTLY as Pulse served it. This is what was signed — prefer it always.

name: pulse_verify_print

at.description: Echoed from the input print, 4th field of the canonical string

fallback_warning.description: Present only when priceText was omitted and price was used instead — flags that JS float formatting could diverge from the signed wire text.

grade.description: Echoed from the input print, 5th field of the canonical string

grade_note.description: Plain-language explanation of what the returned grade means for settlement.

invalid_note.description: Present only when valid is false — explains that the signature does not match the print and it must not be settled against.

key_source.description: Whether the verification key came from cache or a fresh ring fetch

kid_used.description: Key id actually used to verify, resolved from input or the ring

price_field_used.description: Whether priceText (signed) or a String(price) fallback was used

signature_bytes.description: Length of the decoded signature, for sanity-checking the input

symbol.description: Echoed from the input print, 2nd field of the canonical string

valid.description: True only if the signature matches the canonical string exactly

verification.description: States the algorithm and that Pulse is never asked to vouch for a print

title: Pulse Verify Print
